scenes.narration: Templates. Client Libraries — Fundamentals (Part 2 of 2). In this video we review 5 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the syntax used in js.txt and css.txt files to identify source files?
scenes.heading: #base = [root], specifying the path to the root of the client library folder, followed by the file names to merge
scenes.body: The js.txt and css.txt syntax uses a #base directive specifying the path to the root of the client library folder, followed by [file] directives naming the source files to merge into the generated JS and CSS output.

scenes.question: How is the name of the generated merged JS/CSS file determined?
scenes.heading: The node name plus a .js or .css extension, e.g. a node named cq.jquery generates cq.jquery.js or cq.jquery.css
scenes.body: When a client library folder is used, AEM merges the source files into a single JS and CSS file, named after the library node with a .js or .css extension — for example, a node named cq.jquery generates cq.jquery.js or cq.jquery.css.

scenes.question: Where should JavaScript, CSS, and other front-end assets be stored for AEMaaCS front-end development?
scenes.heading: The ui.frontend module of the AEM Project Archetype
scenes.body: For AEMaaCS, it's recommended to store all JavaScript, CSS, and other front-end assets in the ui.frontend module of the AEM Project Archetype, which provides flexibility to use modern web tools.

scenes.question: What does the AEM Project Archetype's build script do with the ui.frontend module's assets?
scenes.heading: It compiles front-end resources into single CSS/JS files and automatically embeds them into a cq:clientLibraryFolder
scenes.body: The AEM Project Archetype can compile front-end resources from ui.frontend into single CSS and JS files, which are then automatically embedded into a cq:clientLibraryFolder in the AEM repository, optimizing delivery.

scenes.question: Why must client libraries be located under /apps, and how are they made accessible?
scenes.heading: It's used to isolate code from content/configuration; a proxy servlet then exposes it via /etc.clientlibs when allowProxy is true
scenes.body: Client libraries must be located under /apps to better isolate code from content and configuration. ACLs are still enforced on the folder, but a proxy servlet allows the content to be read via /etc.clientlibs/ when the allowProxy property is set to true.
